summary: The proposal presents a coherent concept and several clearly stated objectives, but substantial work is needed before submission. The main weaknesses are the horizontally layered schedule, insufficiently measurable deliverables, incomplete AI transparency details, and several smaller formatting and writing issues.

findings.title: Proposal sections are not identified in the AI Transparency Statement
findings.description: The AI Transparency Statement identifies the tools and their purposes but does not specify which proposal sections each tool was used for. Add explicit section names, such as Abstract, Introduction, Problem, Motivation, Objective, Schedule, or Bibliography, and associate the relevant tools and uses with them.

locations.quote: In preparing this proposal, I made use of several AI-based tools across different stages of the writing process. For grammar and style correction, I used Grammarly to identify grammatical errors, improve sentence structure, and refine the overall writing style of my drafts.

findings.title: Iterations are split by horizontal layers
findings.description: The schedule is organized around horizontal system layers rather than vertically integrated, end-to-end features. Reorganize the iterations so that each delivers a usable slice—for example, guideline input through feedback generation to supervisor review in Thesis Management—while incrementally expanding functionality.

locations.quote: Iteration 1 (08.06.2026 - 2 weeks) • Modularize Thesis Management to prepare integration of the feedback module (Objective 4)
Iteration 2 (22.06.2026 - 2 weeks) • Implement core feedback generation pipeline (Objective 1)
Iteration 3 (06.07.2026 - 2 weeks) • Connect feedback tool to Thesis Management (Objective 4)

findings.title: Schedule deliverables lack measurable acceptance criteria
findings.description: Several iteration deliverables are not sufficiently measurable because they do not define an observable output, acceptance criterion, test set, or evaluation result. Replace broad activities with concrete deliverables such as a demonstrable workflow, a specified number of supported guideline formats, a test suite with target coverage, or benchmark results using a defined dataset and metric.

locations.quote: • Modularize Thesis Management to prepare integration of the feedback module (Objective 4)
• Implement core feedback generation pipeline (Objective 1)
• Connect feedback tool to Thesis Management (Objective 4)
• Review the system and check for bugs

findings.title: Schedule includes a documentation task
findings.description: The schedule includes a documentation task. Under the schedule rules, iterations must focus on development and research work; remove this item and replace it with a concrete validation, integration, or research deliverable.

locations.quote: • Documentation

findings.title: High-level objectives are not formatted as bullet points
findings.description: The high-level objectives are presented as a numbered list rather than the required bullet list. Convert objectives 1–4 to bullet points while keeping each objective on one line.

locations.quote:
**1.** Generate Feedback Based on Guidelines
**2.** Highlight Changes Across Iterations
**3.** Compare Prompting Techniques and LLM Models
**4.** Integrate With Thesis Management

findings.title: Remove filler transitions and unsupported superlatives
findings.description: Remove filler transition words where they do not express a necessary logical relation, or replace them with direct connections between sentences. Also replace unsupported superlative expressions with precise, measurable wording or provide evidence for the comparisons.

locations.quote: Moreover, the time spent on repetitive feedback leaves less time for what matters most: helping students with their research and providing feedback on substantive topics.
Additionally, supervisors can provide feedback faster, making the process more scalable.

locations.section: Objective — Compare Prompting Techniques and LLM Models
locations.quote: In addition, privacy regulations and cost require careful consideration of when to use locally self-hosted LLMs versus cloud-hosted ones.

locations.section: Objective — Compare Prompting Techniques and LLM Models
locations.quote: We benchmark which of these options performs best in this setting.
By building on existing processes, the integration causes the least disruption to supervisors and delivers the greatest simplification of their workflow.

findings.title: Introductory paragraph is too short
findings.description: This introductory paragraph is only about four rendered lines long. Expand it with the role and significance of research proposals, or merge it with the preceding paragraph so that the introductory discussion develops a sufficiently substantial unit.

locations.quote: Before starting their research project, students typically write a research proposal. In this proposal, they define the research question and problem they want to explore, outline their methodology, and specify the scope of their work.

findings.title: Feedback-generation paragraph is too long
findings.description: This paragraph exceeds ten rendered lines. Divide the three feedback-generation modes into a short introductory paragraph followed by separate paragraphs for supervisor-only feedback, direct LLM feedback, and the combined supervisor–LLM workflow.

locations.quote: This approach supports several modes of feedback generation. In one mode, no LLM-generated feedback is produced at all and all feedback comes from the supervisor. Alternatively, the student can obtain instant feedback on their proposal or thesis directly from the LLM, while keeping in mind that the supervisor has not reviewed this output. A third mode combines both sources, as illustrated in Figure 2. In this combined mode, multiple specialized agents analyze specific parts of the thesis in parallel. The supervisor then aggregates and reviews the resulting feedback and adds their own feedback. Finally, the supervisor merges both sets and publishes them to the student.

findings.title: Standardize the name of the LLM-based system
findings.description: The envisioned LLM-based system is referred to with multiple terms, including “LLM-powered Reviewer,” “Reviewer,” and “feedback tool.” Define the relationship between these terms and use one consistent name for the same system throughout; if “Reviewer” denotes a distinct component or role, state that distinction explicitly.

locations.quote: As Figure 1 illustrates, an LLM-powered Reviewer works alongside the supervisor, evaluating the thesis against the research group’s writing guidelines and generating automatic formative feedback [NM06].
